clue.text: In the middle of Luton fellows in waistcoats go round making financial provisions for the future

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the waistcoats go round the other pieces, so their letters enclose them

parts.note: in British English a vest can mean a waistcoat (in US usage); vests is the plural
fellows means men

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter, here from Luton

explanation.surface: Men in waistcoats stroll around the centre of Luton, a town north of London, while planning their pensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' has VESTS enclose MEN plus T (the middle of LUTON), giving VESTMENTS after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Investments are money placed now so it returns income later, a provision against future needs.

clue.text: Names of love-torn sisters?

indicators.note: the sisters are torn open so the love can sit inside them

parts.note: nuns are called Sister in religious orders
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about what to call sisters torn apart by a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' splits NUNS so O goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, nouns are the words used to name people, places and things.

clue.text: Go off and trudge in a West country stream

indicators.note: the trudging word sits inside the stream's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in the West Country of England
to plod is to trudge

explanation.surface: A walker sets out and trudges through a river in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe flows through Exeter in Devon; PLOD goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that goes off detonates, bursting violently.

clue.text: Kept in the dark about East European cathedral city ?

indicators.note: the phrase for being kept in the dark goes about the compass point, holding it

parts.note: someone kept in the dark was told nothing; nothing is O, giving TOLD O

explanation.surface: Someone kept uninformed about a cathedral city in the east of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept in the dark' is read as 'told nought', TOLD + O; 'about' wraps that round E. 'East European' looks like one phrase, but East gives only E.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo, in central Spain, is a historic city famous for its great Gothic cathedral.

clue.text: It's not difficult to follow so ready a transcription

indicators.note: a transcription rewrites material in a new form, so these letters are set down rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone praises a written copy of a text for being clear and simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A path that is effortless to take is an uncomplicated route, one with no hardship along it.

clue.text: A tint I blended with a fabulously wonderful leading lady

indicators.note: blending mixes things together, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A colour tint is mixed up to dress a glamorous star actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended' rearranges A TINT I into TITANI, then the second 'a' adds A at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream Titania is queen of the fairies, a lead role from a fable world.

clue.text: What one must do to succeed 5 in business?

definitions.text: What one must do to succeed 5 in business?

parts.words: What one must do to succeed 5 in business?
parts.note: the clue asks what a trader must do to do well on an easy road, that is to thrive in commerce: shift goods for more than they cost

explanation.surface: A question about the secret of commercial success.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 points to 5-down, EASY ROAD, the smooth path to success a trader takes by making money on each sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading so the price received exceeds the cost is the basic way a business makes money.

clue.text: Another version of a decent love story, in short

indicators.note: another version rewrites what is given, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone retells a respectable romance in a briefer form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another version of' shuffles A DECENT together with O (love). 'love story' reads as a romance, but love is only the O.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a brief tale told about a real incident, a short narrative.

clue.text: Having things very much in mind

definitions.text: Having things very much in mind

parts.words: Having things very much in mind
parts.note: read as someone whose thoughts dwell on possessions, wanting to own goods

explanation.definitionFit: A person devoted to acquiring possessions and wealth is focused on worldly goods above spiritual values.

clue.text: Furnish out of pique, maybe

indicators.note: made out of the word pique, its letters reshaped into a new word; 'maybe' marks that

explanation.surface: Someone decorates a room purely from spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' plus 'maybe' tells you to rework the letters of PIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone is to supply or provide them with what they need.

clue.text: Excited Italian describing American ship that came to a tragic end

definitions.text: ship that came to a tragic end

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the anagram goes round the other piece
excited means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An agitated Italian talks about an American ship that sank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' rearranges ITALIAN, and 'describing' has it draw round US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cunard liner Lusitania was torpedoed and sunk by a German submarine in 1915 with great loss of life.

clue.text: Call at the inn just before closing time ?

definitions.text: Call at the inn just before closing time ?

parts.words: Call at the inn just before closing time ?
parts.note: read as a visit to the pub, but really the barman's shout inviting the final round of drinks

explanation.walkthrough: British pubs must stop serving at a fixed hour, and the barman calls this out shortly before.
explanation.definitionFit: The final opportunity to buy drinks before a British pub shuts is announced by the staff.

clue.text: A recess in a Teutonic hermitage

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hermit's cell in Germany has an alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'TeutoNIC HErmitage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow hollow set into a wall, often to hold a statue.

clue.text: Just the thing for getting into a show

explanation.surface: Something ideal for gaining admission to a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the ticket' is an idiom meaning exactly what is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially the ideal thing is called just the ticket; and a printed pass gives admission to a theatre performance.

clue.text: Inventive Red Indian ringing at teatime

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the people's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people (the clue uses a dated term)
taken as written
teatime is four o'clock, written IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An imaginative Native American takes tea at the usual hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Teatime is taken as 4 o'clock, so IV; 'ringing' puts AT plus IV inside CREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone creative has original ideas and makes new things, being imaginative.

clue.text: One kind of tube fare in Rome

definitions.text: One kind of tube fare in Rome

parts.words: One kind of tube fare in Rome
parts.note: read as the price of an underground ticket in Rome, but it is food shaped like tubes eaten in Italy

explanation.walkthrough: 'tube fare' suggests the London Underground (the Tube) and ticket prices; here fare means food.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian pasta comes as short hollow tubes, a staple dish in Rome.

clue.text: Loth to venture from our 13?

indicators.note: made from the letters given, which are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: 13 refers to the answer at 13-across, a word for a recess

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to leave a cosy alcove of theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges OUR together with NICHE, the answer to 13-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking bravery is reluctant to take risks or act boldly.

clue.text: Quietly going ahead and asking for mercy

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
leading means being in front, going ahead of others

explanation.surface: A prisoner steps forward softly and begs to be spared.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleading means begging earnestly, as a condemned person begs for clemency.

clue.text: Ardent sort of aspiration for a place near Dartford

indicators.note: a sort of the word suggests a jumbled form of it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: aspiration is the breathy sound written as the letter H

explanation.surface: Keen ambition is directed towards a spot close to a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges ARDENT into DARENT, then H is added. Dartford is a town in Kent, south-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Darenth is a village in Kent, close to the town of Dartford.

clue.text: How's that for attractiveness?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what you think of their charm.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielders shout 'How's that?' to ask the umpire to give the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer's shout of 'How's that?' asks the umpire for a dismissal; separately the word means allure or charm.

clue.text: Rewarding times for workers

parts.note: read as satisfying moments at work, but literally the dates when wages are handed over

explanation.definitionFit: These are the regular dates on which employees receive their wages.

clue.text: Wild orgy on Tyneside breakwater

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: Tyneside, round Newcastle, is in north-east England, NE

explanation.surface: A riotous party takes place on a sea wall in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges ORGY into GROY, then NE follows; 'on' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out from a beach to check erosion, a kind of breakwater.

clue.text: Extremely low-scoring shot

parts.note: a shot at a target landing in the ... ring scores least; 'Extremely' also hints at the far edge

explanation.walkthrough: In archery and rifle shooting the ring furthest from the bull's-eye scores lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: In target shooting a hit in the outermost ring, far from the centre, earns the fewest points.

clue.text: Rather soon in the date season?

definitions.text: Rather soon in the date season?

parts.words: Rather soon in the date season?
parts.note: read as the start of the time when date palms fruit; the phrase means it is too soon to judge

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's early days' is an idiom meaning it is too soon to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a time at the very beginning of something, too soon for results.

clue.text: Leave Channel ?

parts.note: read as departing over the English Channel, i.e. taking one's leave the French way

explanation.walkthrough: Across the Channel, in France, a farewell is said with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: This French farewell is used when taking leave of someone for good.

clue.text: A catalogue in not very bad shape

indicators.note: something in bad shape is disordered, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A list of goods is found to be in poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad shape' rearranges IN NOT VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a complete itemised list of goods or property, a catalogue.

clue.text: Excuse offered for absenteeism

parts.note: read as a note for missing work, but it is a claim to have been elsewhere at the time of a crime

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word means 'elsewhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accused person's defence that they were somewhere else when the crime took place.

clue.text: Is afraid to face the free-range poultry situation?

definitions.text: Is afraid to face the free-range poultry situation?

parts.words: Is afraid to face the free-range poultry situation?
parts.note: read literally, the hens are outdoors; idiomatically, someone withdraws from a challenge through fear

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means backing out of something through cowardice.
